cards.explanation: The answer is that Paul asks them to pray for his team. He writes, "Finally, brothers, pray for us…" (2 Thessalonians 3:1). The man has a whole letter's worth of things he could ask for, and he asks for prayer. Plain and simple, friends.

The answer is that the word of the Lord spreads quickly and is honored. Paul asks them to pray "…that the word of the Lord may spread quickly and be held in honor…" (2 Thessalonians 3:1). Quickly AND honored, friends. He wants it moving fast and treated with respect.

The answer is True. Paul says the word of the Lord should be held in honor, "…just as it was with you." (2 Thessalonians 3:1). So it was already honored among the Thessalonians. Their own experience is what he compares it to.

The answer is wicked and evil men. Paul says, "And pray that we may be delivered from wicked and evil men…" (2 Thessalonians 3:2). He asks for rescue from people, not from weather or hunger. Short list, clear request, friends.

The answer is False. Paul says, "for not everyone holds to the faith." (2 Thessalonians 3:2). Not everyone, friends. The verse doesn't say everyone holds to the faith, and Paul is honest that some people don't, which is why he asks for prayer about the wicked and evil men.

The answer is that the Lord will strengthen them and guard them from the evil one. Paul says, "But the Lord is faithful, and He will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one." (2 Thessalonians 3:3). Two things, strengthen and guard. And the one doing it is the Lord, not the believers white-knuckling it alone.

The answer is Lord. Paul writes, "And we have confidence in the Lord that you are doing and will continue to do what we command." (2 Thessalonians 3:4). His confidence sits in the Lord, friends. Anybody can say "I believe in you," but Paul puts it somewhere sturdy.

The answer is False. Paul says they "…are doing and will continue to do what we command." (2 Thessalonians 3:4). Are doing, so they've already begun, and will continue. That's a proud-dad kind of sentence, and I love it.

The answer is perseverance. Paul writes, "May the Lord direct your hearts into God’s love and Christ’s perseverance." (2 Thessalonians 3:5). Perseverance means keeping on, which fits believers who are going through hard times. It's the kind of staying power you need in a long bake, friends.

The answer is True. Paul writes, "May the Lord direct your hearts into God’s love and Christ’s perseverance." (2 Thessalonians 3:5). Two things in one line, friends: God's love and Christ's perseverance. Both are in the same prayer.
